subject.title: feat(linux): native gateway transport for Quick Chat — device identity, TLS pinning, ack-driven sends

question: Should the Linux Quick Chat app receive the same direct-local silent-pairing and operator-scoped native-client trust class as the existing native apps, with `dashboard --json` supplying its bootstrap transport data?
rationale: This is a deliberate product and security-boundary expansion, not a mechanical correctness question: it changes which local native clients may create persistent operator devices and how bootstrap credentials cross from the CLI to the app.

options.title: Approve the Linux native trust model
options.body: Accept Linux as a native UI client after Gateway/security-owner review of local-pairing, credential-handoff, and TLS-pinning assumptions, then rebase and land with final-head proof.

options.title: Keep CLI delegation for now
options.body: Retain the existing CLI-backed Quick Chat transport until a broader native-app trust contract is approved.

options.title: Narrow the transport contract
options.body: Allow a native connector only after redesigning the pairing or bootstrap-auth handoff so it does not extend the current silent-pairing trust class.

recommendation.title: Approve the Linux native trust model
recommendation.body: Accept Linux as a native UI client after Gateway/security-owner review of local-pairing, credential-handoff, and TLS-pinning assumptions, then rebase and land with final-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the adjacent merged Linux Quick Chat implementation and authored the proposed Gateway integration, making them the best available routing candidate for the design discussion.
